summary:
La Rioja stands under Spain's national framework: Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, the Law for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGBTI persons (BOE no. 51, 1 March 2023), applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities, including La Rioja. Title II allows adults to rectify their registered sex marker by simple declaration, with no requirement of prior medical diagnosis or treatment, and provides for adaptation of identity documents accordingly; transitory provisions govern rectification applications pending at entry into force.

Under Article 43 of the same statute any person aged 16 or over may request rectification of the gender mention on their own civil registry entry directly before the Civil Registry, an administrative self-identification route that replaced the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis plus two years of medical treatment. Recognition is possible from age 12 under conditions, and the law regulates consent for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16.

Access to sex-separated facilities rests on the gender marker recorded in the civil registry rather than on biological sex, so a visitor's operative document is the basis for facility rules in Spain. This contrasts with the stricter single-sex-space approach being adopted in the United Kingdom on biological-sex lines, where restrictions are applied case by case rather than as a blanket ban.

Other operative provisions reaching a visitor include a ban on non-consensual normalising surgeries on intersex children, expanded assisted reproduction rules, parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples, strengthened sexuality education, and anti-discrimination measures covering healthcare, employment and housing. Same-sex marriage and full adoption rights have been in force since 2005, and legal gender change does not require surgery or sterilisation.

There is no free-standing criminal offence of gender-expression-based hate crime in Spain: the phrase 'gender expression' appears in no article of the Spanish Criminal Code. The hate-speech aggravating circumstance in Article 22.4 and the penalties of Article 510 (one to four years' imprisonment plus a fine of six to twelve months) derive from Organic Law 6/2022, while Ley 4/2023 itself reformed offences against sexual freedom, including Articles 132, 173, 178 to 181 and 189 bis.

Enforcement of the gender-identity aggravation is documented at first-instance level. In July 2026 the Tribunal de Instancia in Vigo applied the transfobia aggravating circumstance for the first time in a misdemeanour case concerning threats sent by WhatsApp to a trans woman, fining the author EUR 300. In a separate case reported on 8 January 2026, a juvenile gang harassed, insulted, beat and filmed a trans person in a park in Valencia to mock them; the only adult defendant received six months' prison and two minors were judged separately.

La Rioja has its own regional layer alongside the national statute. It created a same-sex couple registry in 2010 and in February 2022 passed a regional trans-rights law allowing trans people to self-declare their legal gender; that regional law has applied since 2022 and remains in force alongside Ley 4/2023. La Rioja is also listed among the autonomous communities banning conversion therapies.
tangentialFactors:
Spain's administrative self-declaration regime places it alongside Argentina, Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay. A 2016 survey of 23 countries ranked Spain the most trans-supportive of the group surveyed and the only country where a majority supported unrestricted legal gender designation change; that ranking is a dated baseline predating the 2023 law.

Human Rights Watch, reporting the Congress of Deputies' passage of the Trans Law on 16 February 2023, placed the reform within European and international standards against disproportionate requirements for legal gender recognition, and noted that the provision allowing recognition for children from age 12 proved contentious.

The two enforcement decisions cited above were handed down in Vigo and Valencia, in other autonomous communities rather than in La Rioja. They evidence how Spanish courts apply the gender-identity aggravating circumstance nationally, but they are not a record of incidents inside La Rioja itself.

Two legal layers operate concurrently for a visitor: the regional trans-rights law of February 2022 and the national Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023. Neither displaces the other, so facility access, document adaptation and registry procedure rest on the combined framework rather than on a single instrument.
localsOnly:
La Rioja residents aged 16 or over rectify the gender mention on their own registry entry directly before the Civil Registry by simple declaration under the national law, with no diagnosis, treatment or surgical condition attached; identity documents are adapted to the corrected marker. Applications already pending when the statute entered into force are handled under its transitory provisions.

Residents have been able to self-declare legal gender under La Rioja's regional trans-rights law since February 2022, which continues to apply to them alongside the national statute. The regional same-sex couple registry, in place since 2010, and the regional ban on conversion therapies form part of the resident-facing framework.

The same national law mandates public-policy, workplace, health and education measures, and prohibits LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing, so residents can invoke these protections in ordinary dealings with regional services and employers. Assisted reproduction access, parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples and the ban on normalising surgery on intersex children before consent likewise bind residents directly.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains no La Rioja-specific enforcement record: no documented use of the transfobia aggravating circumstance, no assault or threat case and no discrimination complaint inside La Rioja is sourced here. The incidents cited are from Vigo and Valencia and are presented as national pattern evidence only.

The text of La Rioja's February 2022 regional trans-rights law was not examined directly; its existence, date and self-declaration content rest on secondary reporting. The precise relationship between that statute and Ley 4/2023 in cases of conflict is unresolved on this record.

The scope and enforcement machinery of La Rioja's conversion-therapy ban are not sourced beyond the fact of the ban. Nor is there documentation of documentation-checkpoint practice at airports, hospitals or shelters in La Rioja, or of how regional facilities implement the marker-based access rule.

The 2016 23-country survey predates Ley 4/2023 by roughly seven years and cannot describe current Spanish public opinion.
